name: ob
description: The complete interface implemented by ob, the OpenBindings reference tool. One unbound contract describing everything ob does: creating, inspecting, editing, validating, comparing, and invoking OpenBindings interfaces, plus context storage and environment management. This document carries no bindings or sources; it is the single source of truth from which the per-surface realizations (CLI via usage, server via OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/MCP) are derived, so they cannot drift. An operation that realizes a published OpenBindings interface is keyed by that interface's operation name (e.g. openbindings.kv-store.set), so satisfaction needs no alias; ob's own operations are keyed under the ob namespace (e.g. ob.syncInterface). Aliases appear only where one operation satisfies more than one published interface, as listFormats does.

openbindings.software-descriptor.getInfo.description: Return identity and metadata about ob: name, version, description, homepage, repository, maintainer.

openbindings.binding-invoker.listFormats.description: List the binding formats this instance can handle. One operation satisfies the listFormats slot of every interface that has one, since the answer is the same regardless of which capability is asking.

ob.resolveInterface.description: Resolve an OpenBindings interface from a URL or host. Performs well-known discovery, follows redirects, and synthesizes an OBI from a raw binding spec (e.g. an OpenAPI document) when the target is not already an OBI. Returns the interface and metadata about how it was resolved.

openbindings.interface-creator.createInt.description: Create an OpenBindings interface, optionally from binding source artifacts. Given one or more sources (e.g. an OpenAPI spec, a CLI usage spec), extracts operations, schemas, sources, and bindings into the new OBI; with no sources, produces an empty interface to author by hand.

openbindings.source-inspector.inspectSou.description: Inspect a binding source artifact and report the bindable targets it contains, before any interface is created. Lets tooling show a user what an artifact offers.

ob.createSource.description: Register a binding source reference on an interface and return the modified interface.

ob.deleteSource.description: Remove a source reference from an interface and return the modified interface.

ob.listSources.description: List the source references on an interface.

ob.createOperation.description: Add an operation with the given key to an interface and return the modified interface.

ob.renameOperation.description: Rename an operation and update every reference to it (bindings, aliases) across the interface. Returns the modified interface.

ob.deleteOperation.description: Remove one or more operations and their bindings from an interface and return the modified interface.

ob.listOperations.description: List the operations on an interface, optionally filtered by tag.

ob.syncInterface.description: Re-derive an interface's operations and bindings from its sources' x-ob references and return the synced interface alongside a report of what changed. Local edits that conflict with source changes are surfaced unless overridden.

ob.mergeInterfaces.description: Selectively apply changes from one interface (or from the target's own sources) into another, and return the merged interface alongside a report of what was applied and skipped.

ob.listConflicts.description: List the unresolved conflicts between an interface's local edits and the latest content of its sources.

ob.validateInterface.description: Validate an OpenBindings interface document against the specification. Reports whether it is valid, the declared spec version, and any problems. With strict mode, rejects unknown fields and requires a supported version.

ob.compareInterfaces.description: Structurally compare two interfaces (or one interface against what its sources produce) and report the differences per operation and metadata field, including cross-source drift.

ob.assessCompatibility.description: Assess whether a candidate interface conforms to a target interface and produce a report: per-operation input/output slot status, overall conformance level, and coverage. A report, not a binary verdict.

openbindings.binding-invoker.invokeBindi.description: Invoke a resolved binding via a typed bidirectional I/O frame stream (the binding-invoker frame protocol). The caller streams BindingInvokerInputFrame messages (one `open` carrying the BindingInvocationInput, zero or more `input`, one `close`); the service streams BindingInvokerOutputFrame messages back (zero or more `output`/`input_closed`, then exactly one terminal `complete` or `error`). One shape covers unary, server-streaming, client-streaming, and bidirectional bindings; cardinality is observed by how the caller drives the frames. Missing runtime context fails with a terminal CONTEXT_REQUIRED error carrying ContextRequiredDetails, before any output and any side effect.

openbindings.binding-invoker.prepareBind.description: Preflight a binding: report the context it would require before invocation, without invoking it or causing side effects. Returns ContextRequiredDetails the runtime can resolve proactively, or null when requirements cannot be determined statically. Advisory; invokeBinding's reactive CONTEXT_REQUIRED error is authoritative. When context is supplied, reports only the requirements still unsatisfied by it.

openbindings.operation-invoker.invokeOpe.description: Invoke an operation on an interface via a typed bidirectional I/O frame stream (the operation-invoker frame protocol). Unlike invokeBinding, the caller names an operation (or a specific binding) on a supplied interface, and the invoker resolves the name, selects a binding, validates against the operation's schemas, applies its transforms, and drives the underlying binding invoker. The frame shape mirrors invokeBinding exactly: one `open` carrying the OperationInvocationInput, then input frames and a close; output frames plus a terminal complete or error. Cardinality is observed, not declared, so a request/response and a streaming binding can satisfy the same operation identically. Missing context fails with a terminal CONTEXT_REQUIRED error before any side effect.

openbindings.operation-invoker.prepareOp.description: Operation-level preflight: report the context invoking an operation would require, without invoking it or causing side effects. The by-reference counterpart to prepareBinding. Resolves the named operation (or binding) on the supplied interface to a concrete binding and reports that binding's ContextRequiredDetails, or null when requirements cannot be determined without invoking. Returning null is always conformant. Advisory: invokeOperation's reactive CONTEXT_REQUIRED is authoritative. When context is supplied, the result reports only the requirements still unsatisfied by it.

ob.getContext.description: Get the stored context for a key. Returns the unified context payload (credentials, headers, cookies, environment, metadata in a single opaque map), or null when no context exists for the key.

ob.setContext.description: Create or replace the context for a key. The supplied value fully replaces any existing context (full replacement, not partial update).

ob.deleteContext.description: Delete the stored context for a key. Deleting an absent key succeeds.

ob.listContexts.description: List non-secret metadata summaries for all stored contexts; never returns secret values. Completes the context surface with listing and inspection: the generic kv-store substrate these contexts are stored under (satisfied by getContext/setContext/deleteContext) standardizes only opaque get/set/delete, so this management view is ob's own.

ob.createDelegate.description: Register a delegate: an external binding invoker, reached over exec or HTTP, that handles formats this instance does not support natively.

ob.listDelegates.description: List the registered delegates and the formats each handles.

ob.resolveDelegate.description: Report which delegate handles a given format token.

ob.initializeEnvironment.description: Initialize an OpenBindings environment (the .openbindings/ directory) and return its status.

ob.getEnvironmentStatus.description: Report the status of the current OpenBindings environment, or, when an interface is supplied, that interface's sync report against its sources.

ob.startServer.description: Start a local server that exposes ob's operations over HTTP (and the binding-invoker frame protocol). A foreground, environment-local operation; not meaningfully invoked over a remote transport.

ob.startMCPServer.description: Serve one or more interface URLs as an MCP server, exposing their operations as MCP tools over stdio or HTTP. A foreground, environment-local operation, the MCP sibling of startServer; not meaningfully invoked over a remote transport.

ob.codegen.description: Generate a typed invoker for an interface in a target language (TypeScript or Go). The output is an invoker over the cardinality-agnostic handle, not a cardinality-specific client.

ob.conform.description: Scaffold a target interface so it conforms to a reference interface: add the operations the reference requires and reconcile mismatches, returning the updated target and a report of each change. With dryRun, reports the changes without applying them.

ob.demo.description: Start the bundled demonstration servers (HTTP and gRPC) that showcase one interface satisfied across multiple binding formats. A foreground, environment-local operation, like startServer; not meaningfully invoked over a remote transport.

InterfaceInput.description: Wraps the interface document an operation acts on.

SoftwareInfo.description: Identity and metadata for a piece of software.

FormatInfo.description: Information about a supported binding format.

address.description: Base URL or host to resolve from (e.g. https://api.example.com or localhost:8080).

synthesizedFrom.description: The binding-format token the interface was synthesized from (e.g. openapi@3.1) when the target was not already an OBI; absent for native OBIs.

Source.description: A binding source artifact, referenced by location or carried inline.

location.description: Location of the source (path or URL).

CreateInterfaceSource.description: A binding source to extract operations from.

name.description: Key for this source in the output interface's sources.

location.description: Location to fetch content from (path or URL).

outputLocation.description: Location to reference in the output interface's source.

embed.description: If true, embed content inline in the output interface.

exhaustive.description: True if every bindable target in the source is listed.

ref.description: Reference within the source identifying this target.

operationKey.description: Suggested operation key for this target.

Operation.description: An operation definition as it would appear in an interface.

input.description: JSON Schema for the new operation's input.

output.description: JSON Schema for the new operation's output.

idempotent.description: Whether the new operation is idempotent.

force.description: Prefer source for all conflicts, overwriting local edits.

operations.description: Sync only these operations and their bindings.

sourceKeys.description: Source keys to sync; default all.

pure.description: Strip all x-ob metadata from the result.

SyncResult.description: The synced interface plus a report of what changed. Each list is the set of affected keys.

pure.description: True when x-ob metadata was stripped from the result.

fromSources.description: Derive the source side from the target's own binding sources.

only.description: Scope to a specific source key (requires fromSources).

excludeOperations.description: Exclude these operations from the merge.

ObjectConflict.description: An operation or binding whose local edits conflict with source changes.

FieldConflict.description: One field that differs across the three-way merge of an object.

base.description: The value in the common ancestor.

source.description: The value the source now produces.

strict.description: Reject unknown fields and require a supported spec version.

version.description: The spec version the document declares.

fromSources.description: Compare the baseline against what its binding sources produce.

only.description: Scope to a specific source key (requires fromSources).

DiffReport.description: The differences between two interfaces (or an interface and what its sources produce). Empty operations, metadata, and drift means they are identical.

DriftEntry.description: One operation key produced by multiple sources with differing schemas.

OperationCompatibility.description: Compatibility for a single operation, with per-slot status.

matched.description: Whether a matching operation exists in the candidate.

SlotStatus.description: Compatibility status of an input or output slot.

location.description: Location of the binding source (path or URL).

BindingContext.description: Opaque runtime context for invocation, typically sourced from a context store. Well-known credential fields: bearerToken, apiKey, basic (username/password), accessToken/refreshToken/expiresAt for OAuth. Well-known transport fields: headers/cookies/environment (string-valued objects) and metadata. Implementations and callers MAY add fields; drivers SHOULD ignore fields they don't recognize.

BindingInvocationInput.description: Initial payload carried by the open frame: identifies the binding to invoke and provides context.

BindingInvokerInputFrame.description: One frame from the caller into invokeBinding. The caller streams: exactly one `open` first (carrying the BindingInvocationInput), then zero or more `input` frames, then exactly one `close`.

oneOf.title: open
oneOf.description: Open the invocation. MUST be the first frame on the input stream.

oneOf.title: input
oneOf.description: Write one input value to the underlying binding. The value's schema is the underlying operation's, not this contract's.

value.description: One input value, opaque at this layer.

oneOf.title: close
oneOf.description: Caller signals no more input frames will be sent. Idempotent.

BindingInvokerOutputFrame.description: One frame from the service back to the caller. Zero or more non-terminal frames (`output`, `input_closed`) followed by exactly one terminal frame (`complete` or `error`).

oneOf.title: output
oneOf.description: One output value from the underlying binding. Opaque at this layer.

value.description: One output value, opaque at this layer.

oneOf.title: input_closed
oneOf.description: The binding has closed the input side from its end. Subsequent caller input frames are ignored. Outputs may still flow.

oneOf.title: complete
oneOf.description: Terminal: the binding completed normally. MUST be the last frame.

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: Terminal: the binding failed. MUST be the last frame. Carries a structured InvocationError.

OperationInvocationInput.description: Initial payload carried by invokeOperation's open frame: the interface to act on and which operation (or specific binding) to invoke, plus context.

operation.description: Operation key to invoke. A binding is selected automatically.

binding.description: Binding key to invoke; the operation is derived from it. Mutually exclusive with operation.

OperationInvokerInputFrame.description: One frame from the caller into invokeOperation. Same shape as the binding-invoker input stream, with the open frame carrying an OperationInvocationInput: exactly one `open` first, then zero or more `input` frames, then exactly one `close`.

oneOf.title: open
oneOf.description: Open the invocation. MUST be the first frame on the input stream.

oneOf.title: input
oneOf.description: Write one input value to the operation. Validated against the operation's input schema.

oneOf.title: close
oneOf.description: Caller signals no more input frames will be sent. Idempotent.

OperationInvokerOutputFrame.description: One frame from invokeOperation back to the caller. Same shape as the binding-invoker output stream: zero or more `output`/`input_closed` frames, then exactly one terminal `complete` or `error`. Each output is validated against the operation's output schema.

oneOf.title: output
oneOf.description: One output value from the operation.

oneOf.title: input_closed
oneOf.description: The operation has closed the input side from its end. Subsequent caller input frames are ignored. Outputs may still flow.

oneOf.title: complete
oneOf.description: Terminal: the operation completed normally. MUST be the last frame.

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: Terminal: the operation failed. MUST be the last frame. Carries a structured InvocationError.

InvocationError.description: Structured error carried by an error output frame. Indicates terminal failure of the invocation.

code.description: Machine-readable error code (e.g. ERR_CANCELLED, ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED, ERR_PROTOCOL, CONTEXT_REQUIRED).

details.description: Optional structured details specific to the code. For CONTEXT_REQUIRED, a ContextRequiredDetails object.

ContextRequiredDetails.description: The details payload of a CONTEXT_REQUIRED error, and the return shape of prepareBinding. Enumerates the context the invoker needs. `alternatives` are disjunctive (satisfy ANY one); the requirements within an alternative are conjunctive (satisfy ALL). This OR-of-AND shape captures semantics such as 'OAuth2 OR (apiKey AND clientCert)'.

target.description: The target the binding addresses; the runtime derives a storage key from it.

ContextRequirement.description: One prerequisite that must be satisfied before invocation, resolved into context. `type` names the requirement family (e.g. auth.bearer, auth.oauth2, auth.basic, auth.apiKey, approval.user, config.value); remaining fields are type-specific. A runtime dispatches each requirement to a resolver registered for its type.

durable.description: Whether resolved context MAY be cached under the challenge key and reused (true; e.g. credentials), or MUST be satisfied freshly each time (false; e.g. a one-shot approval). Defaults to true.

Context.description: Opaque per-target context payload: credentials, session state, headers, cookies, environment, metadata, or any other invoker-managed state. Well-known fields include bearerToken, apiKey, basic, headers, cookies, environment, metadata.

ContextSummary.description: Non-secret metadata about a stored context entry. Never includes secret values.

url.description: Context store key (normalized API origin or other stable identifier).

loadError.description: Set if the entry could not be parsed.

urls.description: Interface URLs to expose as MCP tools.

port.description: HTTP port when transport is http (default 8080).

url.description: Base URL the server is listening on.

language.description: Target language for the generated invoker.

package.description: Go package name (Go only; default derived from the interface name).

ConformInput.description: conform input: `interface` is the reference contract whose operations `target` must satisfy; `target` is the interface scaffolded to conform, returned modified as `interface` in the result.

dryRun.description: Report the changes without applying them.

modified.description: Whether the target was changed (false under dryRun or when already conformant).

ConformAction.description: A single change conform made or would make to the target.

operation.description: The operation key the change concerns.

action.description: scaffold (add a missing operation), replace (update a drifted one), skip, or compatible (already conforms).

SourceListEntry.description: A source from the interface's sources map, with its key.

key.description: The source's key in the interface's sources map.

OperationListEntry.description: An operation from the interface's operations map, with its key and the bindings that realize it.

key.description: The operation's key in the interface's operations map.

bindings.description: Keys of the binding entries that realize this operation.

SyncConflict.description: A single conflicting field on an object during sync.

base.description: The value in the common ancestor.

source.description: The value the source now produces.

MergeEntry.description: One operation-level change in a merge, and whether it was applied.

operation.description: The operation key the change concerns.

action.description: The merge action for this entry (e.g. add, update, conflict).
